It supports native `<audio>` files (mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ...) and SoundCloud

ai-chat-chain-of-thought.name: ChainOfThought
ai-chat-chain-of-thought.description:
`ChainOfThought` and its yielded `ChainOfThoughtStep` render a
collapsible list of tool-call-style steps for
[Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat).
The container's own `@open` toggles the whole panel; each step toggles
independently and shows a status icon (success/failure/processing).
ai-chat-chain-of-thought.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel that wraps this chain of thought's steps is open. |
| `@controlled` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, propagated to every yielded step as its own `@controlled`. |
| `@panelId` | `string` |  | ID applied to the content panel `<div>`. |
| `@onToggle` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called whenever `@open` changes after initial render, including externally-driven changes (not just user interaction) — mirrors upstream's `updated()`-driven `chain-of-thought-toggled` event. Passes just the new open state, not upstream's panel element, for consistency with this port's other `onToggle` callbacks (e.g. `ChainOfThoughtStep`). |

## Blocks

- default block: Renders one `<ChainOfThoughtStep>` per step. Yields the step component pre-bound with `@controlled`, mirroring `Layer`'s `WithBoundArgs` pattern for propagating a single arg down an arbitrary number of children.
  - yields `ChainOfThoughtStep` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

| `@onRenameSave` | `(newName: string) => void` |  |  |

ai-chat-chat-shell.name: ChatShell
ai-chat-chat-shell.description:
`ChatShell` is the layout shell for a
[Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat)
window — header, message history, input, and optional history/workspace side
panels. Content is supplied entirely through named blocks; `ChatShell` itself
owns no conversation state.

`@showHistory`/`@showWorkspace` are always-controlled booleans — there is no
uncontrolled/default-open variant, matching upstream's own API.

The `input` block is entirely caller-supplied too — `ChatShell` doesn't own a
text field or send button. The **With prompt line** story composes
`PromptLineShell` + `PromptLine` (upstream's own separate `prompt-line`
component) into it.
ai-chat-chat-shell.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@aiEnabled` | `boolean` |  | Enables AI-specific theming for the chat shell. |
| `@showFrame` | `boolean` |  | Shows a frame border around the chat shell. |
| `@cornerAll` | `CornerStyle` |  | Sets the corner style for all corners. Individual `@cornerStartStart` / `@cornerStartEnd` / `@cornerEndStart` / `@cornerEndEnd` args override this value. Defaults to `'square'`. Upstream renders each corner independently via a per-instance dynamic stylesheet (`CornerManager`). This port only distinguishes "at least one corner is round" vs. "all square" (a single `.rounded` modifier class) — genuinely mixed round/square corners on one shell aren't yet supported. |
| `@cornerStartStart` | `CornerStyle` |  | Controls the start-start corner (top-left in LTR). Overrides `@cornerAll` if set. |
| `@cornerStartEnd` | `CornerStyle` |  | Controls the start-end corner (top-right in LTR). Overrides `@cornerAll` if set. |
| `@cornerEndStart` | `CornerStyle` |  | Controls the end-start corner (bottom-left in LTR). Overrides `@cornerAll` if set. |
| `@cornerEndEnd` | `CornerStyle` |  | Controls the end-end corner (bottom-right in LTR). Overrides `@cornerAll` if set. |
| `@showHistory` | `boolean` |  | Shows the history panel. Always-controlled boolean — matches upstream's `show-history` attribute, which has no `default-show-history` counterpart and no change event, so there's no uncontrolled path to offer (see AGENTS.md §3). |
| `@showWorkspace` | `boolean` |  | Shows the workspace panel. Always-controlled, same shape as `@showHistory`. |
| `@workspaceLocation` | `StartOrEnd` |  | Location of the workspace panel. Defaults to `'start'`. |
| `@historyLocation` | `StartOrEnd` |  | Location of the history panel. Defaults to `'start'`. |
| `@workspaceAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the workspace region. |
| `@historyAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the history region. |
| `@messagesAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the messages region. |
| `@panelOpenedAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when a (non-workspace) panel opens. Accepted for API parity; nothing in this port dispatches the panel open/close events upstream keys this announcement off, since the `panels` block's content is entirely up to the caller here (see class doc). |
| `@panelClosedAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when a (non-workspace) panel closes. See `@panelOpenedAnnouncement`. |
| `@workspaceOpenedAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when the workspace opens. Accepted for API parity; not yet wired to an actual screen-reader announcement in this port (see class doc). |
| `@workspaceClosedAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when the workspace closes. See `@workspaceOpenedAnnouncement`. |
| `@historyShownAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when history becomes visible. See `@workspaceOpenedAnnouncement`. |
| `@historyHiddenAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announcement text for when history becomes hidden. See `@workspaceOpenedAnnouncement`. |
| `@contentMaxWidth` | `boolean` |  | Constrains the input/messages column to a maximum width. When `false`, those slots extend to the full container width. |

ai-chat-code-snippet.name: AiChatCodeSnippet
ai-chat-code-snippet.description:
`AiChatCodeSnippet` is a CodeMirror 6 powered code display/editor: syntax
highlighting, line folding, and a collapse/expand affordance for long
snippets. Exported as `AiChatCodeSnippet` (an existing Carbon React
`CodeSnippet` already occupies the plain name). `@code` is the sole content
source — pass a plain string (update it however you like, e.g. token by
token while streaming a response) and the editor stays in sync via a
throttled diff, not a full reset, so scroll position and selection survive.

CodeMirror itself, and each individual language grammar, is dynamically
imported the first time a snippet actually renders — a page with no
`AiChatCodeSnippet` on it never downloads any of this.
ai-chat-code-snippet.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@code` | `string` |  | The code to display/edit. The sole content source - see the class doc. |
| `@language` | `string` |  | Language used for syntax highlighting (an exact `@codemirror/language-data` name, or a common alias/extension - see `-code-snippet/language-utils.ts`). |
| `@editable` | `boolean` |  | Whether the snippet is an editable surface rather than a read-only display. |
| `@highlight` | `boolean` |  | Enables syntax highlighting (language detection/label-locking still runs either way). |
| `@defaultLanguage` | `string` |  | Fallback language used for empty editable content when nothing else resolves one. Defaults to `'javascript'`. |
| `@detectLanguage` | `boolean` |  | Show the detected language label in the header. When `false` (the default), only an explicit `@language` renders a label. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideCopyButton` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideHeader` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideLineNumbers` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideFold` | `boolean` |  | Hides the fold gutter, removing the ability to collapse/expand code blocks (drops the fold keymap too). |
| `@maxCollapsedNumberOfRows` | `number` |  | Max rows shown when collapsed. `0` (with `@maxExpandedNumberOfRows` also `0`) enables fill-container mode; `Infinity` grows with content instead of scrolling. Defaults to `15`. |
| `@maxExpandedNumberOfRows` | `number` |  | Max rows shown when expanded (`0` = unlimited). Defaults to `0`. |
| `@minCollapsedNumberOfRows` | `number` |  | Min rows shown when collapsed. Defaults to `3`. |
| `@minExpandedNumberOfRows` | `number` |  | Min rows shown when expanded. Defaults to `16`. |
| `@showLessText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@showMoreText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@copyButtonTooltipContent` | `string` |  |  |
| `@foldCollapseLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `@foldExpandLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `@ariaLabelEditable` | `string` |  | Aria-label for the editable surface. `{language}` is replaced with the detected/declared language once locked in. Defaults to `'Code editor'`. |
| `@ariaLabelReadOnly` | `string` |  | Aria-label for the read-only surface. `{language}` is replaced with the detected/declared language once locked in. Defaults to `'Code snippet'`. |
| `@getLineCountText` | `LineCountFormatter` |  | Formats the line-count label. Defaults to `${count} lines`. |
| `@actions` | `ToolbarAction[]` |  | Extra toolbar actions, rendered after the copy button (unless `@hideCopyButton`). |
| `@overflow` | `boolean` |  | Enables responsive overflow on the toolbar - see `Toolbar`'s own `@overflow`. |
| `@onChange` | `(content: string) => void` |  | Fires with the new content on every edit. Only meaningful with `@editable={{true}}` - a read-only snippet never changes its own doc. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

ai-chat-prompt-line-autocomplete.description:
The suggestion overlay for `PromptLine`'s mention (`@`), command (`/`), autocomplete, and starter-prompt Tiptap extensions (see **AI Chat/Prompt line** for building those). Pair one `PromptLineAutocomplete` with exactly one `PromptLine` via the imperative handle from its `@onReady` — typically composed inside a `PromptLineShell`'s `<:autocompleteContent>` block.

Mention and command items always insert into the editor as a chip (a `data-token-type="mention"`/`"command"` node — `disableDirectSend` is forced `true` for these two regardless of config). Autocomplete and starter items default to **sending directly**: clicking one fires `@onItemSend` with its `value ?? label` and never touches the editor at all — the host owns actually sending it (this component carries no chat-domain logic, matching `PromptLineShell`). Set `disableDirectSend: true` on an autocomplete/starters config to switch that trigger's items to the "insert into the editor" path instead, firing `@onItemSelected` (and, for starters specifically, `@onStarterSelected` with the editor's full text) rather than `@onItemSend`.

ai-chat-prompt-line.name: PromptLine
ai-chat-prompt-line.description:
`PromptLine` is the editing surface of the chat input stack, typically composed inside a `PromptLineShell`'s `<:editor>` block. It renders a plain `<textarea>` by default and never statically imports `@tiptap/*` — setting `@rich` (or calling `ensureEditor()` off the handle `@onReady` provides) dynamically loads a small Tiptap runtime chunk and upgrades the surface in place, carrying the text, caret, and focus over losslessly. Both modes share the same `@content`/`@onChange`/`@onSendIntent` contract.

`@content` is always-controlled: typing only fires `@onChange`, so the host keeps the text and hands it back. Press Enter to send (Shift+Enter inserts a newline instead).

`@extensions` accepts plain Tiptap `Extension`s appended to the base Carbon bundle (schema, undo/redo, placeholder, plain-text paste, the Enter/Mod-Enter/Escape keymap) — memoize the array you pass, since a fresh one every render rebuilds the live editor (content, selection, and focus survive; undo history doesn't).

### Mention, command, autocomplete, and starter triggers

`buildCarbonExtensions` (and the individual `carbonMention`/`carbonCommand`/`carbonAutocomplete`/`carbonStarterTrigger` factories it wraps, all under `carbon-components-ember/components/ai-chat/-prompt-line/tiptap/`) build Tiptap extensions you pass through `@extensions` like any other — `PromptLine` itself has no dedicated mention/command/autocomplete/starter args, matching upstream's own `<cds-aichat-prompt-line>`. The extensions only dispatch a bubbling `cds-aichat-trigger-change` DOM event with `{ type, query, triggerOffset }`; **the actual popup is `PromptLineAutocomplete`** — pair it with a `PromptLine` via the imperative handle from `@onReady`.

A command chip (`/summarize`) is prefixed with its trigger character by default; a mention chip (`Jane Smith`) isn't — either default can be overridden per-config or per-item via `showTriggerInChip`.

Mention, command, autocomplete, and starter extensions each react to the *same* document changes and dispatch `cds-aichat-trigger-change` independently — combined on one editor, typing `@` after focusing an empty field can dispatch the starter list's own exit event (`null`) *after* the mention trigger's own opening event. A naive "last event wins" listener can momentarily see a stale `null` and hide its popup even though a trigger is genuinely open. `PromptLineAutocomplete` reconciles this (batches same-tick events by microtask, resolves to the last non-null one) — see the **All triggers** story.
ai-chat-prompt-line.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@content` | `string` |  | Current plain-text value. Always-controlled: typing only fires `@onChange`. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Message'`. |
| `@testId` | `string` |  |  |
| `@autofocus` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Fires with the new value on every input, in either mode. |
| `@onSendIntent` | `() => void` |  | Fires on plain Enter (non-empty field) or Mod-Enter (any field), mirroring upstream's Enter-to-send keymap. Identical in both modes. |
| `@rich` | `boolean` |  | Selects the rich Tiptap editor. Defaults to the textarea. The element lazy-loads Tiptap (a dynamic `import()`, so a chat that never sets this never ships it) and upgrades the textarea to it in place — text, caret, and focus all carry over, so the swap is a same-frame handoff, not a visible reset. The upgrade is **sticky**: once rich, later setting this back to `false` does not downgrade. |
| `@extensions` | `Extension<any, any>[]` |  | Host-supplied Tiptap `Extension`s, appended to the base Carbon bundle (schema, undo/redo, placeholder, plain-text paste, the Enter/Mod-Enter/ Escape keymap) when the rich editor (re)builds. Ignored in textarea mode — setting these alone does not trigger the upgrade. Compared by reference: a fresh array every render rebuilds the live editor (preserving content/selection/focus but resetting undo history), so memoize it rather than passing an inline literal. |
| `@onReady` | `(api: PromptLineApi) => void` |  | Called once, right after mount, with an imperative handle to the surface. |

`DataTable` yields its building blocks already wired to the table: `Toolbar` (with `Content` and the batch-action bar `Actions`), `SearchInput`, `Table`, `Header`, `EachBodyRows` (yielding a `Row` per item), `Column`, `Menu` and `Pagination`. Every `<td>` is automatically linked to its column's `<th>` via the `headers` attribute for screen-reader users.
components-datatable-filtering.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@onSelectionChange` | `(items: T[]) => void` |  |  |
| `@registerState` | `(state: State<T>) => void` |  |  |
| `@search` | `() => Promise<boolean>` |  |  |
| `@state` | `State<T>` |  |  |
| `@items` (required) | `T[]` |  |  |
| `@isLoading` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@title` | `string` |  |  |
| `@description` | `string` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields a hash:
    - `Toolbar`: component
    - `SearchInput`: component
    - `Pagination`: component
    - `Table`: component
    - `EachBodyRows`: component
    - `Column`: component
    - `Menu`: component
    - `Header`: component

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

stories.name: Default
stories.snippet:
<DataTable
  @title="DataTable"
  @description="Filter rows with the toolbar search"
  @items={{ROWS}}
  as |table|
>
  <table.Toolbar as |toolbar|>
    <toolbar.Content>
      <table.SearchInput />
    </toolbar.Content>
  </table.Toolbar>
  <table.Table @size="lg" @useZebraStyles={{false}}>
    <table.Header @headers={{HEADERS}} />
    <table.EachBodyRows as |row|>
      <row.Row>
        <Cells @Column={{table.Column}} @item={{row.item}} />
      </row.Row>
    </table.EachBodyRows>
  </table.Table>
</DataTable>

components-datepicker-datepickerinput.name: DatePickerInput
components-datepicker-datepickerinput.description: The text `<input>` rendered for each field of a `DatePicker`: one for a `single` or `simple` picker, two (start and end) for a `range` picker. Render it through the `DatePicker` block, which yields it already wired to the picker; pass `@value` to the `DatePicker`, not to the input.
components-datepicker-datepickerinput.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  | The id of the `<input>`. Also used to associate the label with the field. Auto-generated when omitted. |
| `@labelText` (required) | `string` |  | The text read by assistive technology and (unless `@hideLabel` is set) rendered above the field. |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Visually hide the label, while still keeping it available to assistive technology. |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  | Placeholder text shown in the field when it is empty. |
| `@pattern` | `string` |  | A regular expression pattern the input's value must match. |
| `@type` | `string` |  | The `<input>` element's `type` attribute. |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Specify the size of the field. |
| `@datePickerType` | `"single" \| "simple" \| "range"` |  | Set by the parent `DatePicker` (`simple` renders no calendar icon unless `@invalid`/`@warn` is set). |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether or not the input should be disabled. |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Whether the field is read-only. Set by the parent `DatePicker` when it is read-only. |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the value is invalid. |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the value is invalid. |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is currently in warning state. |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the control is in warning state. |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  | Provide text that is used alongside the control label for additional help. |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event) => void` |  | Called whenever the raw `<input>` fires a `change` event. `DatePicker` drives the actual value through flatpickr directly on the DOM node; this is for consumers that want the raw text as the user types it. |
| `@onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Called when the field is clicked. |

## Blocks

- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the field. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

stories.snippet:

  @datePickerType="single"
  @readOnly={{@readOnly}}
  as |Input|

    @id={{@id}}

    @hideLabel={{false}}
    @placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    @pattern={{@pattern}}
    @type={{@type}}
    @size={{@size}}
    @disabled={{false}}
    @invalid={{false}}

    @warn={{false}}
    @warnText="Warning message that is really long can wrap to more lines"
    @helperText="Optional helper text"
    @onChange={{@onChange}}
    @onClick={{@onClick}}
  />

components-datepicker.name: DatePicker
components-datepicker.description:
DatePicker lets a user pick a date, or a range of dates, from a calendar dropdown, or type one into a plain field. It wraps [flatpickr](https://flatpickr.js.org/) for the calendar and composes one or two `DatePickerInput` fields, yielded from the block, to render the field(s) themselves.

The calendar dropdown renders inside `DatePicker`'s own container by default, so it stays inside whatever root - shadow or document - the picker itself renders into. Pass a different element as `@appendTo` to redirect it elsewhere instead, e.g. to escape an `overflow: hidden` ancestor.
components-datepicker.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@datePickerType` | `DatePickerType` |  | `simple` renders a plain text field with no calendar. `single` and `range` render a calendar dropdown (backed by flatpickr), for one date or two (start/end) respectively. |
| `@dateFormat` | `string` |  | A flatpickr format string controlling how dates are displayed and parsed. |
| `@value` | `DatePickerValue` |  | The date (or, for `range`, the `[start, end]` dates) to seed the field(s) with. Controlled: later changes to `@value` are re-synced onto the field(s) (via the live flatpickr instance for `single`/`range`, or written directly to the input for `simple`) - see `syncValue`. Accepts anything flatpickr's own `defaultDate`/`setDate` accept (a `Date`, a date string, a timestamp, or - for `range` - an array of two). |
| `@minDate` | `DateOption` |  | The minimum selectable date. |
| `@maxDate` | `DateOption` |  | The maximum selectable date. |
| `@allowInput` | `boolean` |  | Flatpickr prop passthrough: whether the field(s) can be edited by typing directly, in addition to picking from the calendar. |
| `@closeOnSelect` | `boolean` |  | Whether the calendar dropdown closes as soon as a date is picked. |
| `@appendTo` | `HTMLElement` |  | The DOM node flatpickr's calendar dropdown is appended into. Defaults to the picker's own container element, so the calendar always lands in the same root (shadow or document) the picker itself renders into - flatpickr's own default of `document.body` would otherwise make the calendar escape a shadow root, where your styles don't reach it. Pass an explicit node to redirect it elsewhere instead (e.g. to escape a `overflow: hidden` ancestor). |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Whether the field(s) are read-only. A read-only picker has no calendar and cannot be typed into. |
| `@short` | `boolean` |  | Renders the compact/short variant. |
| `@light` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `DatePickerChangeHandler` |  | Called whenever the selection changes. |
| `@onOpen` | `DatePickerChangeHandler` |  | Called when the calendar dropdown opens. |
| `@onClose` | `DatePickerChangeHandler` |  | Called when the calendar dropdown closes. |

## Blocks

- default block: Yields `DatePickerInput`, pre-bound to this picker's `@datePickerType` and `@readOnly`. Render one for `simple`/`single`, two (start, then end) for `range`.
  - yields `DatePickerInput` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

stories.name: Default
stories.snippet:
<DatePicker
  @datePickerType="single"
  @dateFormat={{@dateFormat}}
  @value={{@value}}
  @minDate={{@minDate}}
  @maxDate={{@maxDate}}
  @allowInput={{@allowInput}}
  @closeOnSelect={{@closeOnSelect}}
  @readOnly={{@readOnly}}
  @short={{@short}}
  @onChange={{@onChange}}
  @onOpen={{@onOpen}}
  @onClose={{@onClose}}
  as |Input|
>
  <Input
    @labelText={{if
      (isRange args.datePickerType)
      "Start date"
      args.labelText
    }}
    @placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
    @size={{@size}}
    @disabled={{@disabled}}
    @invalid={{@invalid}}
    @invalidText={{@invalidText}}
    @warn={{@warn}}
    @warnText={{@warnText}}
    @helperText={{@helperText}}
  />
  {{#if (isRange args.datePickerType)}}
    <Input
      @labelText="End date"
      @placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
      @size={{@size}}
      @disabled={{@disabled}}
      @invalid={{@invalid}}
      @invalidText={{@invalidText}}
      @warn={{@warn}}
      @warnText={{@warnText}}
      @helperText={{@helperText}}
    />
  {{/if}}
</DatePicker>

components-dropdown.name: Dropdown
components-dropdown.description:
`Dropdown` is a single-select field that opens a listbox of items on click. It renders Carbon's `ListBox` markup directly - the menu is a plain descendant of the field, positioned with Carbon's own CSS - and manages its own open/highlight state internally.

Items can be any value: `@itemToString` turns one into its label (the default is `String(item)`), or a block can render each item.
components-dropdown.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  | The id of the underlying field button. Also used to derive the ids of the label and menu, so the ARIA wiring between them stays consistent. Auto-generated when omitted. |
| `@items` (required) | `T[]` |  | The list of items to choose from. |
| `@titleText` (required) | `string` |  | The field's label, rendered above the control. |
| `@label` (required) | `string` |  | Placeholder text shown in the field when nothing is selected. |
| `@itemToString` | `(item: T) => string` |  | Convert an item to display text. Used both for the field button's `title` attribute and, when no item block is supplied, as the default rendering of each menu item. Defaults to reading a `label` property off the item, falling back to an empty string. |
| `@selectedItem` | `NonNullable<T>` |  | The currently selected item (controlled). Wins over internal state whenever it is defined. |
| `@initialSelectedItem` | `NonNullable<T>` |  | Seeds the initially selected item for the uncontrolled case. |
| `@onChange` | `(data: { selectedItem: T \| null; }) => void` |  | Called whenever the selection changes, with the newly selected item. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the control should be disabled, or not. |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the control should be read-only. A read-only field button remains focusable but cannot be opened or changed. |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the currently selected value is invalid. |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the value is invalid. |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is currently in warning state. |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the control is in warning state. |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  | Provide text that is used alongside the control label for additional help. |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Visually hide the label, while still keeping it available to assistive technology. |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Specify the size of the Dropdown. |
| `@type` | `"default" \| "inline"` |  | `default` renders the standalone field; `inline` lays the field out next to its label (via flex layout classes) and suppresses the helper text row. The label itself is always rendered - use `@hideLabel` to visually hide it. |
| `@direction` | `"top" \| "bottom"` |  | The direction the menu should open in. |

## Blocks

- default block: Customize how each item renders in the menu. Falls back to `itemToString(item)` when no block is supplied. The field button's own text always uses `itemToString`, matching React's default behaviour when `renderSelectedItem` is not passed.
  - yields `item` (`T`)
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the field. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

components-fileuploader.name: FileUploader
components-fileuploader.description:
`FileUploader` lets a user upload one or more files via a button that opens the native file picker, showing every selected file with the same `@filenameStatus`. It's the simple case; for a real upload flow — where files progress through their own `uploading` → `complete`/`edit` states independently, and users can drag and drop files onto the page — compose `FileUploaderDropContainer` and `FileUploaderItem` directly (see the drag-and-drop example applications).

`FileUploader` yields a `clearFiles` action that resets the selected-file list, e.g. once a caller has finished uploading every file — it's the only supported way to reset the picker without destroying/recreating the component.
components-fileuploader.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@accept` | `string[]` |  | Specify the types of files that this input should be able to receive |
| `@buttonKind` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "ghost" \| "danger" \| "danger--primary" \| "danger--ghost" \| "danger--tertiary"` |  | Specify the type of the underlying `FileUploaderButton` |
| `@buttonLabel` | `string` |  | Provide the label text read by screen readers for the upload button |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether file input is disabled |
| `@filenameStatus` (required) | `"complete" \| "edit" \| "uploading"` |  | Specify the status applied to every selected file |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Provide a description for the status icon, read by screen readers |
| `@labelDescription` | `string` |  | Specify the description text of this FileUploader |
| `@labelTitle` | `string` |  | Specify the title text of this FileUploader |
| `@maxFileSize` | `number` |  | Maximum file size allowed in bytes. Files larger than this are marked invalid |
| `@multiple` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the component should accept multiple files to upload |
| `@name` | `string` |  | Provide a name for the underlying `<input>` node |
| `@onAddFiles` | `(event: Event, data: { addedFiles: FileUploaderAddedFile[]; }) => void` |  | Called after files are added, before they're marked invalid/filtered |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event, data: FileUploaderChangeData) => void` |  | Called each time the selected-file list changes |
| `@onClick` | `(event: Event) => void` |  | Called each time a selected file's status icon is activated |
| `@onDelete` | `(event: Event, data: { deletedFile: FileUploaderFileItem; remainingFiles: FileUploaderFileItem[]; }) => void` |  | Called when a selected file is removed (only reachable when `@filenameStatus` is `'edit'`) |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "small" \| "field"` |  | Specify the size of the FileUploaderButton, from a list of available sizes |

## Blocks

- default block: Yields a `clearFiles`-style action that resets the selected-file list, e.g. after a successful upload
  - yields `clearFiles` (`() => void`)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

elements-grid.name: Grid
elements-grid.description:
The 2x Grid is a flexible, 16-column grid system that can be used to build custom layouts. Carbon ships two layout engines for it, and `Grid` renders either one:

- **Flexbox grid** (the default, `@mode="flexbox"`) — a `Grid` renders one or more `GridRow`s, and each `GridRow` renders one or more `GridColumn`s. See *Elements/FlexGrid*.
- **CSS Grid** (`@mode="css-grid"`, these stories) — there are no rows; columns are direct children of the `Grid`. This mode additionally supports subgrids, percentage spans, and explicit `start`/`end` placement.

`Grid` yields `Grid`, `Column`, `Row` and `ColumnHang` components that are already bound to the surrounding grid's mode, so the mode is only picked once.

### Column span shorthand

`GridColumn` accepts a value for each breakpoint (`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xlg`, `max`):

- `true` — the column takes up an equal share of the remaining space
- a `number` — the column spans that many columns
- an object like `{{hash span=4 offset=2}}` — the column spans `span` columns and is offset by `offset` columns

In `css-grid` mode a column additionally accepts a percentage (`'25%'`, `'50%'`, `'75%'`, `'100%'`) and `start`/`end` grid lines.
elements-grid.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@align` | `GridAlign` |  | Specify grid alignment. Default is center. Only applies when `mode` is `css-grid`. |
| `@condensed` | `boolean` |  | Collapse the gutter to 1px. Useful for fluid layouts. Rows have 1px of margin between them to match gutter. |
| `@fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Remove the default max width that the grid has set |
| `@mode` | `GridMode` | `'flexbox'` | Which layout engine to use. `flexbox` renders `cds--grid`/`cds--row`/ `cds--col-*`, `css-grid` renders `cds--css-grid`/`cds--css-grid-column`. |
| `@narrow` | `boolean` |  | Container hangs 16px into the gutter. Useful for typographic alignment with and without containers. |
| `@subgrid` | `boolean` |  | Render as a subgrid of a surrounding CSS Grid instead of as a new grid. Set automatically for the `Grid` yielded from another `Grid`. |
| `@withRowGap` | `boolean` |  | Add a row gap to the grid that matches the current gutter size. |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `grid` (`GridBlock`)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

elements-grid-gridcolumn.name: GridColumn
elements-grid-gridcolumn.description:
A column of the 2x Grid. Render the `Column` yielded by `Grid` (or `GridSettings`), which already has the grid's `@mode`: in the CSS Grid it's a direct child of the `Grid`, in the Flexbox grid it goes inside a `GridRow`.

Each breakpoint arg (`@sm`, `@md`, `@lg`, `@xlg`, `@max`) takes `true` (an equal share of the remaining space), a number of columns, or an object like `{{hash span=4 offset=2}}`. In `css-grid` mode a column also takes a percentage (`'25%'` ... `'100%'`), `start`/`end` grid lines, and a breakpoint-independent `@span`. See *Elements/Grid* for examples.
elements-grid-gridcolumn.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@mode` | `GridMode` | `'flexbox'` | Which grid engine the surrounding `Grid` uses. Normally inherited by invoking the `Column` yielded from `Grid`, but can be set explicitly when a column is rendered on its own. |
| `@sm` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `sm` breakpoint (up to 671px). This breakpoint supports 4 columns by default. |
| `@md` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `md` breakpoint (up to 1055px). This breakpoint supports 8 columns by default. |
| `@lg` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `lg` breakpoint (up to 1311px). This breakpoint supports 16 columns by default. |
| `@xlg` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `xlg` breakpoint (up to 1583px). This breakpoint supports 16 columns by default. |
| `@max` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify column span for the `max` breakpoint. This breakpoint supports 16 columns by default. |
| `@span` | `ColumnSpan` |  | Specify a constant column span, start, or end value that does not change based on breakpoint. Only applies in `css-grid` mode. |

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

`Icon` renders a Carbon SVG icon. Use the generated icon components from `carbon-components-ember/icons` (e.g. `<Bookmark @size={{16}} />`), which load the SVG for the requested size on demand, or register an SVG from `@carbon/icons` with `registerIcon(name, svg)` and render it with `<Icon @icon="name" />`.

Passing `@onClick` renders the icon inside a ghost button and shows a loading state while the (optionally async) handler runs.

components-layer.name: Layer
components-layer.description:
The `Layer` component renders content on a specific Carbon layer. Each layer has a set of token values associated with it, which other components (like `Tile`) key off of to determine their own background. You can use these tokens directly, or use contextual tokens from Carbon's styles package like `$layer` or `$field`.

`Layer`s can be nested up to three levels deep; past that, the level stays clamped at the third level. Ember has no equivalent of React's ambient `LayerContext`, so a bare `<Layer>` always renders as the first level of nesting; to nest `Layer`s more than one level deep, use the component yielded to the block, which is pre-bound to the correct next level:

```hbs
<Layer as |L|>
  ...
  <L>...</L>
</Layer>
```

components-menu.name: Menu
components-menu.description:
Menu is a low-level building block for rendering a floating list of actions; `OverflowMenu` and context menus are built on top of it. It's a controlled component: pass `@open` and toggle it from `@onClose`/your own trigger. Compose it out of `MenuItem`, `MenuItemDivider`, `MenuItemGroup`, `MenuItemRadioGroup`, and `MenuItemSelectable`.

By default the Menu renders into `document.body`; `@target` renders it into another element. `@x`/`@y` position it; passing both edges of a trigger (`[x1, x2]`/`[y1, y2]`) lets it flip to the other side when it doesn't fit. Clicking a leaf item, pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd>, or moving focus outside the menu all call `@onClose`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Pass a node inside your own root when the Menu is rendered in a shadow root, otherwise it escapes into the light DOM where your styles don't reach it. Submenus aren't portaled - they inherit this as their positioning origin instead. |
| `@x` | `number \| [number, number]` |  | Specify the x position of the Menu. Either pass a single number or an array with two numbers describing your activator's boundaries ([x1, x2]). |

components-popover.name: Popover
components-popover.description:
`Popover` is used for triggering a pop-up next to a trigger element, typically a button, in a given direction. It is a controlled component: the consumer owns the `@open` argument and toggles it (usually from the trigger's click handler), while `Popover` calls `@onRequestClose` whenever the user clicks outside of the popover or presses <kbd>Escape</kbd> while focus is inside the popover content.

The trigger element and `PopoverContent` are both yielded as plain children of `Popover`.
components-popover.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `PopoverAlignment` |  | Specify how the popover should align with the trigger element. |
| `@alignmentAxisOffset` | `number` |  | **Experimental:** Provide an offset value for alignment axis. Only takes effect when `autoAlign` is enabled. Not currently implemented in this Ember port. |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | The element type to render the outermost node as. |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | Will auto-align the popover on first render if it is not visible within the viewport (or `autoAlignBoundary`, if provided). |
| `@autoAlignBoundary` | `HTMLElement` |  | Specify a bounding element to be used for autoAlign calculations. The viewport is used by default. |
| `@backgroundToken` | `"layer" \| "background"` |  | Specify the background token to use. Default is 'layer'. |
| `@border` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a border should be rendered on the popover. |
| `@caret` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a caret should be rendered. |
| `@dropShadow` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a drop shadow should be rendered on the popover. |
| `@highContrast` | `boolean` |  | Render the component using the high-contrast variant. |
| `@isTabTip` | `boolean` |  | Render the component using the tab tip variant. |
| `@onRequestClose` | `() => void` |  | Specify a handler for closing the popover. The handler should take care of closing the popover, e.g. changing the `open` argument. Called when the user clicks outside of the popover or presses Escape while focus is inside the popover content. |
| `@open` (required) | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the component is currently open or closed. |

utilities-resizer.name: Resizer
utilities-resizer.description:
A draggable (and keyboard-operable) handle placed between two sibling elements. By default `Resizer` resizes its previous and next DOM siblings directly as it's dragged; pass `@onResize` to take full control instead (for example, to drive a CSS Grid's `grid-template-columns`). Any content passed to the default block is rendered inside the handle, which is useful for a custom drag icon.

Drag the handle with a mouse, or focus it and use the arrow keys (hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> for larger steps, or press <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd> to jump to a boundary). Double-clicking the handle resets the siblings to the size they had when it was inserted.

By design, the resting handle is a subtle `border-subtle`-colored 4px bar, much more visible on hover/focus (`border-interactive`). Carbon's docs suggest enhancing the trigger cue with a pseudo-element or custom children if needed; every story here widens the hit area with an invisible `::before`.
utilities-resizer.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

The Stack component is a useful layout utility in a component-based model. This allows components to not use margin and instead delegate the responsibility of positioning and layout to parent components.

Stack uses the spacing scale from the Design Language in order to determine how much space there should be between items rendered by the Stack component. It also supports a custom `@gap` argument which will allow a user to provide a custom value for the gap of the layout (a number from 1 to 13 picks a step of the spacing scale; a string sets any CSS gap value). components-tooltip.name: Tooltip
components-tooltip.description:
Tooltips display additional information upon hover or focus. The information should be contextual, useful, and nonessential. A tooltip is attached to the element yielded in its default block and shows after a short delay on hover, or immediately on keyboard focus. Pressing `Escape` dismisses it.

Use `@label` when the tooltip names the trigger (exposed as `aria-labelledby`), or `@description` when it adds extra information (exposed as `aria-describedby`). For rich content, use the `:content` block instead. Placement is controlled with `@align`.
components-tooltip.apiDescription:
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "top-left" \| "top-start" \| "top-right" \| "top-end" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-right" \| "bottom-end" \| "left-bottom" \| "left-end" \| "left-top" \| "left-start" \| "right-bottom" \| "right-end" \| "right-top" \| "right-start"` |  | Where the tooltip is placed relative to the trigger |
| `@label` | `string` |  | Label text identifying the trigger. It names the trigger element through `aria-labelledby` (use it for icon-only triggers). |
| `@description` | `string` |  | Description text for the trigger, linked through `aria-describedby` |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | Will auto-align the tooltip on open if it is not visible within the viewport (or `autoAlignBoundary`, if provided). |
| `@autoAlignBoundary` | `HTMLElement` |  | Specify a bounding element to be used for autoAlign calculations. The viewport is used by default. |
| `@closeOnActivation` | `boolean` |  | Close the tooltip when the trigger is activated (click, Enter, Space) |
| `@defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Render the tooltip open on initial render |
| `@dropShadow` | `boolean` |  | Render a drop shadow on the tooltip |
| `@enterDelayMs` | `number` |  | Delay in ms before the tooltip shows on hover |
| `@highContrast` | `boolean` |  | Render with the high contrast theme |
| `@leaveDelayMs` | `number` |  | Delay in ms before the tooltip hides after the pointer leaves |

## Blocks

- default block: The trigger element the tooltip is attached to
- `<:content>`: Custom tooltip content, used instead of

components-treeview.name: TreeView
components-treeview.description:
TreeView is used to render a hierarchical list of nested items that can be expanded or collapsed. `TreeView` and each node yield a bound `TreeNode` component that can be nested arbitrarily deep to build out the tree; select or activate a node by clicking on it.

By default only a single node can be selected at a time. `@multiselect` allows selecting additional nodes by clicking while holding <kbd>Cmd</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>. `@onSelect` is called with the array of selected node ids and the node that triggered the change, and `@onActivate` with the id of the node that received keyboard/click focus.

A disabled node can't be selected or focused (it is removed from the tab order) but still renders, dimmed; on a parent node its toggle caret stays usable so its descendants remain reachable.

components-ui-shell-header.name: UIShell
components-ui-shell-header.description:
The UI Shell is the structural framework of an application that houses navigational elements and page content, so users can move through an application consistently and predictably. Its `shell` block yields a `Header` (top bar with the product name, navigation, and global actions), a `Nav` (top-level navigation links and `HeaderMenu`s), a `Sidenav` (left-hand navigation panel), a `Switcher` and a `HeaderContainer`; the `content` block is the page content.

The `Header` yields a `GlobalAction` into its `headerGlobal` block (icon buttons for search, notifications, the app switcher, ...) and a `HeaderPanel` into its `headerPanel` block. The `Sidenav` block yields `Menu`, `Divider`, `SideNavHeader`, `SideNavDetails`, `SideNavIcon` and `HeaderSideNavItems`, and its `footer` block a `Footer` toggle; wire the toggle to the same `@open`/`@onToggle` state as the `Header`'s menu button (or use `HeaderContainer`, which manages it).
